4. The case of the defendant No. 5 was that his father Chandra Kumar Pal was .the owner of 11.77 acres of land of Khatian Nos. 30 and 32 (from amongst the property as described in schedule 'A') and that his father died leaving him and another as sons and his brother; sold his share in the aforementioned property to him and that he and his brother sold 1-26 acres of land to some others. It is also the case of the defendant that neither he nor his brother executed the deed. of exchange in the form of irrevocable power of attorney and that the alleged deed of exchange in the form of power of attorney is forged, fraudulent and fabricated and that the plaintiffs were never the owners and possessors of the property described in schedule 'B' and that he and others had never exchanged their properties as described in. schedule 'A' with the property described-in schedule 'B'. It was also contended that the plaintiffs were never the inhabitants of Tripura State and that they being the inhabitants of Noakhali used to go to Tripura State for seasonal employment in an agriculture firm. The further contention of the defendant No.5 is that the property of Khatian Nos. 30 and 32 cannot be treated as enemy property. 

 5. The case of the defendant No.6 was that his father Puma Chandra Pal was the owner of the land recorded in khatian Nos. 29, 94, 100 and 255 as mentioned in schedule 'A' and that his father died leaving 3 sons including him and that his 2 brothers upon transferring their shares to him left the then East Pakistan and living in West Bengal and that his brothers were never in the Tripura State and that he and his brothers had never executed the power of attorney for the purpose of exchanging schedule 'A' land for 'B' schedule land and that the power of attorney is forged, fabricated and fraudulent and thus his property cannot be treated as enemy property. 

 6. The case of the defendant Nos. 7-12 was that part of the land of Khatian Nos. 30, 50, 52, 53, 55,95 and 94 as mentioned in schedule 'A' belonged to Raj Kumar Pal, Rajani Kumar Pal, Chandra Kumar Pal and Ram Sundar (Kumar) Pal, that Raj Kumar Pal died leaving 3 sons-defendant No.9, defendant No. 10 and another by name Anukul Chandra Pal who transferred his share to the defendant Nos. 9 and 10 and left for India, Rajani Kumar died leaving 2 sons-defendant No.7 and another by name Gopal Pal who transferred his share to the defendant No.7. Chandra Kumar died leaving 3 sons defendant No. 8 and two others by name, Chitta Ranjan Pal and SushiI Pal and the said two brothers ie Chitta Ranjan Pal and Sushil Pal, transferred their shares to defendant No.8 and left the then East Pakistan for India, Ram Kumar Pal died leaving 4 sons-defendant Nos. 11, 12 and two others by name Harihar and Fani Bhusan Pal and that Harihar and Fani Bhusan transferred their share to the defendant Nos. 11 and 12 and left the then East Pakistan for India. It is the case by this set of defendants that they are in possession of their land acquired by inheritance and purchase and that their property as described in schedule 'A' to the plaint cannot be treated as evacuee or enemy property and that they had never executed the power of attorney in the form of deed of exchange in respect of schedule 'A' property for the property described in schedule ‘B’.
